assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing by synthesis with reversibly terminated fluorescent nucleotides on clustered single molecules is a truly simple, chemistry-driven idea that became a game-changer: it collapsed sequencing cost by orders of magnitude and reshaped biology and medicine. Consequences are exceptionally broad and already realized.
assessment.attribution: The core Solexa chemistry traces to Balasubramanian and Klenerman, who conceived and developed it in Cambridge. Others credited (Rothberg for pyrosequencing and 454, Mayer, Ju) contributed parallel or related platforms; with a three-person cap, the Cambridge pair gives the cleanest and most defensible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: two decades of dominant use, independent platforms and clinical adoption. Timing is not premature; the main question is whether the field is seen as a chemistry rather than a physiology or medicine prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to separate sequencing-by-synthesis from competing technologies such as pyrosequencing and nanopores
Exact historical priority among Solexa, Lynx and 454 contributions is taken from general knowledge and not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers are a completely new class of solar material that reached silicon-competitive efficiencies within a decade; this is the kind of new material with immediate consequences that I would call a game-changer, in the spirit of the MOF prize.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka introduced perovskites as sensitizers in 2009; Park delivered the first solid-state device with substantial stability and efficiency in 2012; Snaith showed the meso-superstructured and planar architectures with high efficiency. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis made important contributions; priority choices among six names are difficult and contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency and reproducibility are firmly confirmed by many groups. Long-term operational stability and commercial deployment remain unproven, so the case is strong but possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Stability, lead toxicity and scale-up are unresolved
Credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel and Seok is disputed and I rely on recollection of the timeline

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials deliver near quantum-mechanical accuracy at force-field cost, opening reaction dynamics, materials and condensed-phase simulation to time and length scales that were out of reach. As a simulation person I judge this a real methodological step change, and it complements recognition of AlphaFold and earlier multiscale work.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello (2007) introduced high-dimensional neural network potentials with symmetry functions; Csányi and Bartók developed Gaussian approximation potentials and the SOAP descriptor. Weinan E, von Lilienfeld and others are also credited, but three names suffice for the foundational methods.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and validated against ab initio benchmarks, yet transferability, extrapolation and uncertainty issues are still being worked out; the field is still moving fast and a prize may be a few years early.
uncertainties: Whether the field has stabilized enough for a clear lasting contribution
Attribution between neural network and kernel approaches and the role of foundation models

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base to another without double-strand breaks, a conceptually new chemistry-on-DNA approach that has already reached patients. It follows the CRISPR prize but is a distinct, clearly novel step with quantified consequences.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conception and development of cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainee scientists on the two classes. For a one-prize slot, Liu alone is the clear intellectual driver, and this avoids splitting credit with a candidate that shares his name (prime editing).
assessment.maturity: Clinical results are accumulating and many labs have confirmed efficiency and specificity, though long-term safety and off-target profiles are still being studied.
uncertainties: Overlap with the prime editing candidate if recognized together
Long-term clinical safety evidence is incomplete

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Practical exchange-correlation approximations, notably the PBE generalized gradient approximation, are the workhorse of computational chemistry and materials science. Impact is enormous and I value theory that connects quantitatively to experiment.
assessment.attribution: Perdew developed the GGA family and is the central figure; Burke and Ernzerhof co-authored PBE. Truhlar and Yang made major contributions to other functionals, and Becke and others outside this list also shaped practical DFT, so credit is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of use and benchmarking make maturity unquestionable, but Kohn's 1998 prize recognized DFT itself, so a second DFT recognition needs a clear argument.
uncertainties: Competing claims on functional development (Becke, Lee-Yang-Parr, not on this list)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns the ubiquitin system into a drug modality via heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, a new paradigm in pharmacology with clinical consequences emerging.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) conceived the original PROTAC concept in 2001; Ciulli made structure-based VHL ligands that enabled modern PROTACs. Handa, Ito and Kim relate to thalidomide and cereblon, a compound discovery that may need separate recognition.
assessment.maturity: Several drugs are in late-stage trials but approvals are limited, so real-world consequences are still developing.
uncertainties: Late-stage clinical outcomes not yet decisive
Unresolved credit among PROTAC and molecular glue discoveries

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a simple, general, widely used method in pharmaceuticals and materials, and this candidate is a mature successor to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic amination with ligand design and mechanism; Kosugi and Migita earlier demonstrated tin-amide coupling, which is a priority issue. Two names make a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Very mature; decades of use, though possibly viewed as an extension of an already awarded field.
uncertainties: Priority of earlier tin amide couplings

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened mild radical chemistry with a simple energy source and spread through synthetic and medicinal chemistry; widespread consequences are already clear.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and MacMillan reported key 2008-2009 contributions; Nicewicz, König, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi also contributed, and MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize, so priority and fairness are difficult.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed and industrially adopted, though the discovery is somewhat diffuse and the field still evolving.
uncertainties: MacMillan is already a laureate, which may argue against him
Priority is distributed among many groups and earlier work
